Subject: Processing territory routing and subprocessor channels

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking my meeting yesterday. As we prepare for procurement I need two concise things we can include in the RFP: a simple map of where Redwood routes inference requests (by default) and a list of any subprocessors that could receive data or tokenized payloads during processing.

Specific questions:
- If our traffic originates in EU or UK, will requests stay within EU/UK data centers or is there default routing to the US?
- For hosted API customers (no VPC), which subprocessors might see request data (cloud providers, monitoring, analytics, vector DB partners)?
- For Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments, what guarantees/capabilities do we have to keep data in-region?
- Do you have a short evidence bundle (diagram + subprocessor list + SOC 2) we can attach?

We are trying to finalize a controls appendix by EOD Friday — anything you can share that is vendor-ready would help.

Best,
Priya
Head of Security & Privacy

Hi Priya — appreciate the clear list. High level answers below, and I'm attaching a compact evidence bundle (PDF + CSV) that you can pass to procurement. If you need more formal signed attestations we can route you to our security team; I'll loop in Marcus for anything that requires SOC artifacts.

Short answers (TL;DR):
- Default (Hosted API): Requests are routed to the nearest healthy Redwood edge and may traverse regions for capacity. By default, hosted traffic is served out of our operational regions (US, EU) with smart routing for latency; that means payloads may cross borders unless the customer requests region pinning.
- Dedicated / Private: We offer per-customer region pinning and VPC private deployment options — these keep processing confined to the selected region and avoid cross-border routing.
- Subprocessors (hosted): primary cloud infra (AWS, GCP), managed logging/metrics provider (Logwise Analytics), CDN/edge partner (FastEdge), and optional vector search partners used only if customers enable those integrations. See attached CSV for the full list and contact scope.
- Evidence bundle: attached "inference-processing-map.pdf" (visual of routing and fallbacks), and "redwood-subprocessors-2027-11.csv" (current subprocessors and purposes). SOC 2 report and more detailed network flow diagrams are available on request and require an NDA for the full redacted copy.

If you want strict in-region guarantees on hosted traffic we recommend either:
1) Dedicated capacity in the EU region (we reserve capacity and pin processing), or
2) Redwood Private (VPC) deployed into your cloud tenancy / on-prem and configured for EU-only routing.

Let me know which approach HealthLytics prefers and I'll follow up with a short statement you can drop into the contract appendix.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales (Security Lead)
Redwood Inference
